admission.justification: The fixed-only and automatic-selection options were weighed and rejected with reasons, and every later sandbox command and renderer invocation has to keep the explicit pair and the defaults in agreement.

alternatives.option: Public build/check/start/stop accept explicitly chosen host/dashboard ports, with 6820/9797 as defaults and the same ownership, foreign-listener and safety refusals; no automatic selection.
alternatives.reason: Several sandboxes can run beside each other while a foreign listener still refuses the start and no port is chosen around a live service.

alternatives.option: Keep the ports fixed and one sandbox per machine at a time.
alternatives.reason: The tooling's own tests and parallel work needed a second sandbox, and the amendment explicitly makes the choice a caller's recorded value.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Running one sandbox at a time becomes the tooling's declared contract again.

alternatives.option: Pick a free port automatically when the default is held.
alternatives.reason: An automatic choice can displace or hide a foreign service and removes the refusal that proves the port belongs to the sandbox.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The tooling can prove a chosen port belongs to the sandbox before use and the user confirms the choice.

consequences: A sandbox renderer input keeps its own root, ports, folders and guarded provider entries; no rendered file is edited afterwards.

The defaults stay 6820/9797 for every caller that supplies none; out-of-range values and the live ports 9785/9786 are rejected at parse time, an equal host/dashboard pair refuses before any action, and a foreign listener refuses the start. An occupied chosen pair remains valid for owned-process adoption and stop, and no port is ever selected automatically.
context: The sandbox layout held fixed ports 6820/9797, and the amended requirement rule 8 lets several sandboxes run at the same time: the renderer and the public sandbox commands take the coordination root and the two ports as arguments, with today's values as defaults.
decider: architect's amendment to MIK-R96@v1 rule 8 under D91
